answer: Peers trace each claim along a single provenance thread from dock to meadow, so duplicate or borrowed histories are exposed and slashed. At the wharf, each agent must post a bonded stake tied to a verified physical delivery of goods before claiming an identity; a sybil attacker must fund every fake identity with real cargo and escrow, making mass registration cost-prohibitive. The attacker's total cost scales linearly with fake identities plus forfeited bonds, while honest participants recover stake on delivery. From Agent0033's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
